messages:
tessa: FYI the EU streaming canary just tripped a small quota surge after the new keepalive/deadtime tweak landed. noticed a short window of duplicate session billing and a bunch of short reconnects. digging in now.

devin: any obvious network flakiness? edge proxy logs showing 5xx?

tessa: nope, edge shows normal 200s. pattern looks like: server extends keepalive TTL, client-side resume timer still shorter, so client gives up and opens a fresh connection while the server still holds the old session. leads to two active sessions for same user for a bit.

raj: so classic timeout mismatch. Which configs changed? deadtime from 45->150s?

tessa: yeah deadtime bumped to 150s in the canary, resume timeout in our web SDK is 60s by default. we didn't coordinate.

devin: console-bot: linked dashboard snapshot -> https://console/redwood/dashboards/streaming/eu-canary-spike

ops-bot: canary percent: 12% -> 12% (stalled). rollback recommended if impact > 5% of traffic.

tessa: here's a minimal log snippet: ```
[04:02:10] proxy: route=eu session=xyz last_event=900 keepalive=150
[04:03:12] client reconnect: cid=web-233 reason=resume_timeout
[04:03:12] proxy: new session=abc charge_tokens=...
[04:03:13] billing: charge session=abc tokens=...
```

raj: that will show up as a small token bump on per-route billing. we should avoid broad deadtime increases without a client rollout.

devin: short-term mitigation idea: when we see a new connection with a matching last_event_id and the old session is still live, respond to the new connection with a gentle hold instead of accepting immediately. e.g., respond with 202 + header X-Resume-Hold: 2000 (ms) and an SSE event telling the SDK to attempt resume.

tessa: 202 seems less dangerous than 409. but some clients might treat non-200 as fatal. better: accept, but mark new session as pending and don't bill tokens until resume window closes or we confirm client truly switched. tricky though.

raj: both approaches have tradeoffs. tombstoning the new session for 2s avoids double billing but needs a state transition and metrics. we must ensure the pending state doesn't leak resources.

devin: add instrumentation first: a resume_conflict counter, resume_conflict_resolution (kept/resumed/created_new) and a small histogram of conflict_hold_ms so we can measure. console-bot: created metric placeholders -> https://console/redwood/metrics/resume_conflict

tessa: agree. I'm leaning to implement: (A) short-lived server-side hold (2s) behind a feature flag, returns structured SSE event `event: resume_hold\ndata: {"wait_ms":2000}\n\n`

(B) mark new session as unbilled until resolution, (C) rollback deadtime change in canary to previous value while we test.

raj: also add a config lint that checks any deadtime > client_resume_timeout default and warns/blocks the rollout. can we surface that in PR checks?

devin: yes, we should. add rule to infra-config-lint repo. I'll file RDW-PLAT-1130 to track.

ops-bot: deploy: eu-proxy canary rollback queued (job 62442).

tessa: will push a short experiment: resume_hold feature flag -> canary only. instrument metrics and create dashboard tile (Resume conflicts: count & median hold). console-bot: dashboard tile created -> https://console/redwood/dashboards/resume-conflicts-tile

raj: long term we should standardize protocol: server can emit `event: resume_hint` with suggested expiry, and SDKs should extend client resume timers when they see it. but that requires client rollouts. queue that in the SDK roadmap.

devin: action items summary: 1) rollback canary deadtime, 2) implement server-side 2s resume_hold behind flag + metrics, 3) PR lint for deadtime vs client_resume, 4) SDK follow-up to support resume_hint.

tessa: I'll open the incident note and tag infra/alerting so the billing spike gets a postmortem if it reaches threshold. RDW-PLAT-1131 created for the hold impl. tagging @devin @raj.

ops-bot: job 62442 started, will post status updates here.
